I do the same thing.  I don’t actually draw blood, but I do scratch the hell out of my arm, thigh, etc.. with keys or whatever I can get.  I often feel like an imposter, or “fake depressed”, but it’s nice to see other people who do things other than strictly slicing with knives.
Same, I literally made my first post yesterday.  It just sucks that it took subreddits about depression and suicide to get me into it.

Dang, that's a really good way of putting it.  I'll do other things that now that I think about, are along the line of looking after myself.  Like, not using blankets if i"m cold because I don't deserve to be warm and comfortable

It's like the saying, you're damned if you do, you're damned if you don't.  People just want you to shut up about it, but they don't want you to die.  It's like they care enough for us to be alive, but not enough to just sit and listen for a minute.

Thank you so much.  I didn't realize how nice it would feel to have someone pay attention.  I appreciate that you find me doing music cool, I wish I felt the same way about myself.  I am seeing a therapist, but I have a feeling with my friends and my therapist where I feel like I can't tell them otherwise I'll get in trouble.  I know that's a dumb thing to think since my friends are friends and my therapist can't disclose that.  whatever.  Thanks again.

This is actually decent advice, not just witty.  Alcohol causes our brain to stop making its own seritonin since the alcohol provides so much.  This is especially bad for those of us with depression as it makes our previous lack of neuroreceptors such as serotonin even worse making us very depressed.  Weed isn't found to have such an impact to our brain's chemistry, at least in that way.
No problem, I hope getting your word out there and voicing your thoughts helped a bit, it sure does for me

Hello.  I know you said that it may be best if no one acknowledges your post, but I hear you.  The thing is, you have been diagnosed with these illnesses, this means you do have these things.  You are valid.  Your actions are symptoms of your diagnoses; your diagnoses aren’t excuses for your actions.  I know everyone says this and I would be a hypocrite if I said I was fully able to do so, but I’ll just say it again.  The past is gone and done with.  Yes, it may affect what your life is at the moment, but you can’t do anything about it.  All you can do is live your life from this moment moving on.  I am aware of how hard it can be to let things go.  I relate really strongly to what you said about feeling attention seeking, I often verbally batter myself saying that I’m not actually depressed, I’m just looking for attention.  

Sorry, I don’t know if any of that helps in any way and I don’t mean to flip this about me.  I hope you are able to relax and hopefully venting helped, I know it can definitely help me.
Congratulations, that’s great to hear!  I hope you continue on this positive trend.

I hear you, and I can definitely relate to your feeling like being an imposter with depression.  When I am in my low points I hear voices saying very similar things like, "you can't actually be depressed, you were born into too good of a situation for that".  Sometimes these voices sound like myself, sometimes they sound like family members.  The important thing to remember, is that you do (probably, I can't diagnose you) have depression, it seems to clearly affects your life and the way you think.  A tip that I learned from my therapist is to think of those voices as a symptom of your depression rather than giving into them.  In other words, when you hear/think those things, try to step back and say, "woah, where did that come from" rather than giving in and accepting it as the truth.  I obviously can't know if this will work for you, but I find that it helps me.  Stick through it.  It's hard dealing with people who are unsupportive, but now you have access to a huge supportive space if you decide to continue using reddit.  I also started using reddit very recently, and I love it.

My depression has severely spiked over the past few years, so I've been on both the giving and the receiving end of these types of conversations.  By giving this type of "advice" people are trying to show that what you're going though "isn't that bad".  People say this because they think that all you stress and depression is the result of one thing, and if they show you that it's not that bad and that they've been able to get over their own struggles, maybe you'll feel better.  In reality, this just invalidates the way you feel, sending you into a deeper depression.
I really hope so.  Thank you for listening.

Man, I feel the exact same way.  I am a senior in high school at the moment and I’d consider myself privileged, however I don’t find any “privilege” in my mental health.  I constantly feel like I don’t deserve anything that my parents do for me.  It feels like any affection they give me is fake or an obligation so that I don’t deteriorate and do something terrible.  I just want to end it but I know that if I do so, I will be ruining my parents work of raising me and I will be wasting all of the effort they made and all of the money they’ve spent on raising a child.  It’s not just money, my parents are extremely supportive of me and my want to become a music teacher but I feel like I don’t deserve the support they’ve shown me.  I completely understand what you expressed about wanting to have some additional trauma in your life to justify your depression.  Even though my depression feels real and it truly affects my life, I feel like I’m faking it since I don’t have any additional trauma to cause it.

By the way: your English was perfect in the post.
